hudson.model.StringParameterDefinition.name: subject_type
hudson.model.StringParameterDefinition.description: for vast majority of studies, this will be Human.

hudson.tasks.Shell.command:
#!/bin/bash
### assume etl role aws sts assume-role --duration-seconds 900 --role-arn arn:aws:iam::736265540791:role/dbgap-etl --role-session-name "s3-test" > assume-role-output.txt
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=`grep AccessKeyId assume-role-output.txt | cut -d ':' -f 2 | sed "s/[ ,\"]//g"` export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=`grep SecretAccessKey assume-role-output.txt | cut -d ':' -f 2 | sed "s/[ ,\"]//g"` export AWS_SESSION_TOKEN=`grep SessionToken assume-role-output.txt | cut -d ':' -f 2 | sed "s/[ ,\"]//g"`
#pulls metadata.json for given study
aws s3 cp s3://avillach-73-bdcatalyst-etl/${study_abv,,}/decoded_data/${study_id}_${study_abv,,}_metadata.json . #add subject_type metadata key to all concepts in metadata.json jq --arg subject_type "$subject_type" '[.[] | .metadata += {"subject_type": $subject_type}]' ${study_id}_${study_abv,,}_metadata.json > tmp.json #pushes metadata.json back to s3 aws s3 cp tmp.json s3://avillach-73-bdcatalyst-etl/${study_abv,,}/decoded_data/${study_id}_${study_abv,,}_metadata.json
